resolved_conflicts.explanation: The December 2017 review gives 245 acres in one passage and 250 acres in another for the Town's acquisition; the story says about 250.
A 1932 newspaper item already calls it the fire lookout tower, and a 1949-1950 state entry says a new tower was built, so the story gives no date for the first tower.

notes_for_editor: Tower history rests on the Eastern US Lookouts page, which quotes Vermont Forest Service biennial reports, the Rutland Daily Herald (1932) and the Burlington Free Press (1968, 1973). No source gives tower height, a demolition date, or whether footings remain, and no source says whether the tower site is open to visitors, so the story says so. The 1973 razing was agreed, not confirmed as done. The 1920s cabin date is approximate. The 2017 review is almost nine years old; the Town of Essex plan for the land may have changed since. The geocaching page for the site was not used. Access is left out of the facts for that reason. Checked 2026-10-10: the review's own acreages do not reconcile with an 88% shrink from about 800 acres (the same review gives 410 acres still privately owned, 250 acres re-acquired by the Town and 90 acres held by the school district), so the story attributes the 88% figure to the review. 'The Trustees' in the 1973 Burlington Free Press item is read as the village trustees, since the village owned the land.
